project.name: Belis Bell
project.one_liner: Online store for washroom and cleaning products in Ghana, serving households and businesses plus institutional buyers such as banks, schools, and government and private companies.

intent.label: Product
intent.value: Online store with a business-supply (B2B) side

intent.label: Primary users
intent.value: Institutional buyers (banks, schools, government, private companies) and general shoppers

intent.label: Usage
intent.value: Heavy contact: ordering, quotes and conversations all day

intent.label: Primary job
intent.value: Find the right product, get a price or quote, and order with confidence

intent.label: Platform
intent.value: Responsive web store, full features on phone and desktop

intent.label: Reference
intent.value: Owner-supplied home page mockup (structure only); the owner supplies all images

decisions.title: Online store for two audiences
decisions.value: One store serves everyday buyers and institutional accounts. Same catalogue, different paths: quick checkout for individuals, quotes and account ordering for institutions.
decisions.rationale: Belis Bell sells washroom and cleaning products and also supplies banks, schools, and government and private companies.

decisions.title: Responsive web, full parity on phone
decisions.value: One responsive web app. Phone gets everything the desktop gets: browsing, quotes, checkout, account, order history. No native app in v1.
decisions.rationale: Used on desktop and phone, and you asked for everything on mobile.

decisions.title: Slow-network tolerance
decisions.value: Lean pages, responsive compressed images, skeleton loading, retryable requests, cart and quote drafts that survive a dropped connection.
decisions.rationale: You flagged slow or patchy internet.

decisions.title: Use in the field, on the move and on shared screens
decisions.value: Large touch targets, strong contrast and larger base type (17px body). Works at a desk, on a phone in a store room, and projected in an office.
decisions.rationale: Contexts chosen: desk, on the move, in the field, shared screen, low bandwidth.

decisions.title: Mixed software comfort
decisions.value: Plain language, one clear action per screen, no jargon. Repeat buyers get shortcuts such as reorder and saved lists.
decisions.rationale: Comfort level: mixed.

decisions.title: Conversation-led buying
decisions.value: Talking to a person is part of the flow: WhatsApp click-to-chat and call buttons on product and quote pages, and a quote thread that carries messages, not just a form.
decisions.rationale: Main activity chosen was communicating, with all-day use. Local B2B buying in Ghana often runs through WhatsApp and phone.

decisions.title: High-stakes ordering
decisions.value: Orders and quotes have a review step, a clear confirmation, an order reference, and an audit trail. Cancelling or editing after submit is deliberate and logged. Undo is not the main safety net.
decisions.rationale: Mistakes cost money.

decisions.title: Trustworthy, friendly, premium tone
decisions.value: Calm, reliable and polished, with warm plain-language copy. Premium through restraint and photography, not gold or heavy effects. No em dashes in UI copy.
decisions.rationale: Feel words chosen: trustworthy, friendly, premium.

decisions.title: Editorial visual direction
decisions.value: Serif display type for headings, paper-toned neutrals, generous whitespace, product photography treated like magazine pages.
decisions.rationale: Editorial was the closest gut pick. Superseded: you selected Fresh and Bright and asked for the Supply Master look instead (PG-025).

decisions.title: Teal accent
decisions.value: Teal is the single accent for primary buttons, links and focus. Status colours stay separate. Every teal used for text or buttons meets 4.5:1.
decisions.rationale: Teal picked; suits water, cleanliness and hygiene. Superseded: the supplied logo sets the brand colours (PG-029).

decisions.title: Soft elevated surfaces
decisions.value: Product cards, quote panels and summary boxes sit on soft shadows. Elevation is reserved for things you act on; page sections stay flat.
decisions.rationale: Soft elevation picked.

decisions.title: Light and dark themes
decisions.value: Follows the device. Light is the designed default (paper-toned); dark is a full second palette, not an inversion.
decisions.rationale: Both themes chosen.

decisions.title: Top bar with mega-menu navigation
decisions.value: Sticky top bar: logo, search, account, cart, and a Buy for Business link. A category mega-menu on desktop; a full-screen category drawer on phone. No sidebar.
decisions.rationale: Top bar chosen; the reference site uses a category mega-menu for a large catalogue. Superseded: the owner mockup sets the header and navigation (PG-034).

decisions.title: Content mix: photos, product grids and copy
decisions.value: Home follows a fixed section order: announcement bar, header, nav row, split hero (photo with headline beside a 2x2 cluster of coloured feature tiles), category pill tabs, product carousels, brand spotlight, three ways to shop tiles, core category tiles, featured partner picks, trust counter, brand in focus, all brands A to Z, footer. Buying guides and hygiene advice sit as a lower strip. Copy and images are Belis Bell's own.
decisions.rationale: Section arrangement taken from the reference at your request; content is original. Superseded: the owner mockup sets the home page structure (PG-033).

decisions.title: WCAG 2.2 AA plus extended needs
decisions.value: AA baseline with full keyboard operation, screen-reader labelling and live regions for cart and quote changes, a low-vision mode (text scaling to 200% without breakage, no reliance on colour), and layouts that tolerate text expansion and RTL.
decisions.rationale: Keyboard, screen reader, low vision and multi-language needs all selected.

decisions.title: Brand identity starts fresh
decisions.value: No existing brand guide. Belis Bell gets a wordmark, colour system and photography style as part of this build, all defined in the approved direction.
decisions.rationale: Brand answer: starting fresh. Superseded: a logo was supplied (PG-030).

decisions.title: supplymaster.store as structural reference
decisions.value: Borrow the structure that works for supply retail: category mega-menu, Buy for Business quote path, delivery and pay-on-delivery messaging, trust counters, FAQ. Do not copy its visual identity, layout details or copy.
decisions.rationale: Given as a note in the workshop. Superseded: you asked to copy the visual style and section arrangement, not just structure (PG-026).

decisions.title: Buy for Business path
decisions.value: A dedicated path for institutions: request a quote from a cart or a list, upload a requirements sheet, get a quote thread, then approve it into an order. Repeat orders reuse past quotes.
decisions.rationale: Institutional supply is half the business and quote-led buying is how institutions procure.

decisions.title: Core screen set
decisions.value: Home, category, product, search results, cart, checkout, quote request, quote thread, account (orders, saved lists, addresses), order tracking, buying guides, about and contact, FAQ.
decisions.rationale: Standard store plus the B2B path.

decisions.title: Product page built for trust
decisions.value: Large photo with zoom, pack size and unit price, stock status, safety and usage notes, downloadable spec or safety data sheet where relevant, WhatsApp button, and add-to-cart plus add-to-quote.
decisions.rationale: Institutional buyers compare pack sizes and need documentation.

decisions.title: Empty, loading and error states
decisions.value: Skeleton loaders, helpful empty states (empty cart suggests categories), and plain errors that say what happened and how to fix it, with a retry.
decisions.rationale: Patchy connections make this visible often.

decisions.title: Payment model
decisions.rationale: Changes checkout, account screens and the security design. Decide before build.
decisions.question: How will customers pay?

options.label: Pay online
options.hint: Mobile money and card at checkout

options.label: Online plus pay on delivery or invoice
options.hint: Individuals pay online, institutions get invoiced

options.label: Orders and quotes only
options.hint: No online payment; you confirm and invoice by hand

decisions.value: Pay online

decisions.title: Institutional account model
decisions.rationale: Decides whether institutions log in with contract pricing or just request quotes.
decisions.question: How should institutions buy?

options.label: Request a quote each time
options.hint: No special accounts; you reply with pricing

options.label: Approved business accounts
options.hint: Login, agreed pricing, order history, approval by you

options.label: Quotes first, accounts later
options.hint: Launch with quotes, add accounts in a later phase

decisions.value: Request a quote each time

decisions.title: Public prices
decisions.rationale: Affects catalogue cards, search and SEO.
decisions.question: Should prices be visible to everyone?

options.label: Retail prices public, bulk on quote

decisions.value: Prices shown to all

decisions.title: Supply Master visual language
decisions.value: Adopt the reference's visual style: deep-toned header, footer and buttons on a light page, a photo-led hero with dark overlay and large white headline, coloured feature tiles with photos, rounded (12px) buttons and cards, product carousels with a full-width add-to-cart button, Figtree-style semibold headings, generous section titles centred over light grey-tinted bands. Belis Bell's own palette, logo, photography and copy are used throughout.
decisions.rationale: Your note: copy the visual style, not the content. Superseded: the owner mockup replaces the Supply Master visual language (PG-036).

decisions.title: Section arrangement follows the reference
decisions.value: Home and category pages keep the reference's section order and rhythm (see PG-014). No text, product photos, logos, brand names or partner names are copied. Nothing implies affiliation with Supply Master.
decisions.rationale: Your note, plus the reference belongs to another company. Superseded: the owner mockup replaces the reference arrangement (PG-033).

decisions.title: Deep teal takes the place of the reference's navy
decisions.value: Header accent, buttons, announcement bar and footer use deep teal (#0a5f61). Feature tiles rotate teal, coral (#b4491f), green (#1f6b3d) and ink (#12303a), each with white text above 4.5:1. Reject this if you want the reference's navy instead.
decisions.rationale: You picked teal earlier and chose Fresh and Bright; keeping the hue keeps Belis Bell distinct from the reference. Superseded: the palette now comes from the logo (PG-031).

decisions.title: Ways-to-shop tiles and category set
decisions.value: Three big entry tiles under the product carousels: Shop Products, Buy for Business (quotes) and Washroom Solutions (curated packs for a whole washroom). Core category tiles: Washroom Supplies, Cleaning Chemicals, Cleaning Equipment, Hygiene and Waste, Dispensers and Fittings. Final names come from the real catalogue.
decisions.rationale: Mirrors the reference's three-ways and core-categories blocks for a washroom and cleaning catalogue. Superseded: the mockup uses six category cards and audience cards (PG-033).

decisions.title: Brand colours come from the logo
decisions.value: Blue is the single action colour (#006cbc, white text 5.4:1). Deep navy (#044788) is for the announcement bar, footer and headings on tinted bands. Green (#43b14a in the logo) is a brand accent for badges, highlights and illustration only. Text and buttons use a darker green (#2b7d32, white text 5.1:1) because the logo green fails contrast. Teal is dropped.
decisions.rationale: Colours sampled from the supplied logo; the earlier teal pick predates it. Superseded: the mockup uses green for primary buttons (PG-036).

decisions.title: Logo supplied
decisions.value: Use the updated Belis Bell logo (blue B with cart, spray bottle, soap and tissue; blue and green wordmark; descriptor 'Cleaning Supplies & More'; line 'For homes, businesses and institutions'). Saved as brand/logo-primary.webp; the first version is archived. The header uses a compact lockup and the full logo appears in the footer and about strip. The file is a 1254px raster on white with a light halo, so a transparent PNG or SVG and a horizontal lockup are needed before build.
decisions.rationale: You shared an updated logo in chat. Its descriptor now covers cleaning as well as washroom products.

decisions.title: Blue, navy and green in the Bright Supply layout
decisions.value: Header, buttons and links use blue. The announcement bar and footer use navy. Feature tiles rotate blue, navy, green (#2b7d32) and ink (#0a1d33), each with white text above 4.5:1. Dark theme uses a light blue primary (#6ab7f5) on a deep navy-black ground.
decisions.rationale: Applies the logo palette to the approved section layout. Superseded: the palette is now defined in PG-036.

decisions.title: Mock data for the first build
decisions.value: The first build uses clearly labelled mock data for products, prices (GHS), stock, categories, brands, delivery figures, the trust counter and customer content. Mock data lives in one seed file, is never presented as real, and is removed before launch. Payments run in provider test mode only until the security gate signs off live keys.
decisions.rationale: You asked to use mock data for prices, products and everything else for now.

decisions.title: Home page structure follows the owner's mockup
decisions.value: Sections in this order: (1) header; (2) hero with a small eyebrow label, a three-line two-tone headline, one supporting sentence, two buttons (Shop Now, For Businesses) and a row of four trust points (Fast delivery across Ghana, Quality products, Trusted support, Secure payments); (3) Explore Our Range: six category cards, each with a photo, name and an arrow; (4) a blue promo banner with headline, one sentence, a Shop Now button and a photo on the right; (5) Solutions for Every Space: three audience cards (Homes, Businesses, Institutions) with a photo, icon, title and one line; (6) Popular Products: a carousel of product cards with price and Add to Cart; (7) Why Choose Belis Bell: four points with icons (Quality Brands, Fast Delivery, Great Value, Dedicated Support); (8) a second banner, Clean Spaces Start Here, with Shop Now and Contact Us; (9) footer.
decisions.rationale: Supplied by the owner as a home page mockup. The mockup gives structure only; the owner supplies all images.

decisions.title: Header, navigation and footer follow the mockup
decisions.value: Header: logo on the left, six text links (Home, Shop, Categories, For Businesses, About, Contact) and three icon buttons (Search, Account, Cart with a count). On phones the links move into a menu. Footer: logo and tagline with social icons, then Quick Links, Customer Support and Contact columns, then a copyright line with Privacy Policy and Terms links.
decisions.rationale: Shown in the owner's mockup.

decisions.title: The owner supplies all imagery
decisions.value: Photos and illustrations are supplied by the owner. The site is built with named image slots (listed in docs/IMAGES.md) and neutral placeholders until each image arrives. No images are generated by the developer, and none are taken from other websites. Photos that show other companies' branded packaging need the owner's confirmation that showing them is allowed.
decisions.rationale: Owner: 'I will supply the visuals images I want'. The mockup shows recognisable third-party brand packs, which need rights confirmed.

decisions.title: Visual style follows the mockup, with an accessible green
decisions.value: Light page with white and very pale blue-grey surfaces; rounded cards (16px) with a soft shadow; pill-shaped buttons, filled green for the main action and white with a navy outline for the second; headlines in navy with blue and green emphasis words; small spaced-out capital eyebrow labels; deep navy banners (#00346e and #002b61) with the photo on the right; deep navy footer (#001b38). The main button green is #2b7d32 with white text (5.1:1), because the mockup's bright green #3fa80c fails contrast with white text (3.1:1). Blue #006cbc is for links and small accents. The logo's bright green is for icons and highlights only. Dark theme stays.
decisions.rationale: Colours sampled from the mockup, adjusted for WCAG AA.

decisions.title: Structure pages for the navigation
decisions.value: Build the pages the navigation points to as structure with clearly labelled mock text: Categories (all categories), For Businesses (how quotes work, audience cards, a Request a quote button that is switched off until the quote flow is built), About, and Contact (details plus a WhatsApp link; no form yet). Footer links to FAQ, Shipping and Delivery, Returns and Refunds, Payment Methods, Track Order, Privacy Policy and Terms appear only when the page has real content. Social icons appear only with real links. The address, phone, email and opening hours in the mockup are treated as mock until supplied.
decisions.rationale: Every nav link should go to a real page, and policy and legal text needs real content from the owner.

decisions.title: Promises in the trust row are the owner's to confirm
decisions.value: The trust row and the Why Choose section make promises: fast delivery across Ghana, quality brands, great value, dedicated support and secure payments. Shown as mock copy until the owner confirms each is true. Secure payments is shown only once Paystack live payments are approved.
decisions.rationale: Claims must be things Belis Bell can keep.

directions.name: Paper and Teal
directions.tagline: A calm supply catalogue with editorial polish.
directions.fit: Matches your picks exactly: editorial, teal, soft elevation, top bar, trustworthy and premium. Feels like a well-run supplier that institutions trust, and still warm enough for households.
directions.tradeoffs: Serif headings and airy spacing use more scroll length. Needs good product photography to earn the premium feel.

foundation.Navigation: Sticky top bar with category mega-menu
foundation.Primary interaction: Category browse, product grid, add to cart or quote
foundation.Mobile strategy: Full parity, category drawer, sticky add-to-cart
foundation.Animation: Subtle, image fade and card lift, reduced-motion safe

directions.name: Procurement Desk
directions.tagline: Quote-first and built for institutional buyers.
directions.fit: Puts Buy for Business at the centre: a sharper, denser catalogue with pack-size tables, saved lists and reorder. Best if institutions bring most of the revenue.
directions.tradeoffs: Less editorial warmth; households may find it businesslike. Needs the account model decision to be answered as accounts.

foundation.Navigation: Top bar plus persistent account and quote strip
foundation.Typography: IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Serif for headings
foundation.Primary interaction: Product tables, bulk quantity entry, saved lists
foundation.Mobile strategy: Full parity, tables collapse to stacked rows

font.mono: IBM Plex Mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace

directions.name: Bright Supply
directions.tagline: Clean, photo-led home page in the Belis Bell logo colours.
directions.fit: Follows the owner's mockup: clear hero, category cards, audience cards, product carousel and two navy banners. Friendly for households and credible for institutions.
directions.tradeoffs: Depends on the owner's photography for most of its appeal. Until the photos arrive, the placeholders make the page look plain.

foundation.Navigation: Header with logo, six text links and search, account and cart icons
foundation.Primary interaction: Hero with two buttons, category cards, audience cards, product carousel with Add to Cart
foundation.Mobile strategy: Full parity, tiles stack, carousels swipe, category drawer
foundation.Animation: Carousel scroll and gentle hover lift, reduced-motion safe

risks.text: High-stakes ordering with payments and institutional data means security must be designed before the first commit (payment handling, account access, quote data). Next gate: Opskeep/Elliot.
Premium editorial look depends on real product photography. Weak or inconsistent photos undermine trust more than in a plain design.
Extended accessibility scope (screen reader, low vision, multi-language and RTL) adds test effort across every screen.
Payment, institutional account and price visibility decisions (PG-022 to PG-024) change checkout, accounts and data model. They must be answered before build.
The reference site is another company's identity. Only its structure is borrowed; visuals and copy must be original.
Following another company's visual style closely can look like a clone. Original logo, photography, wording and palette are required, and nothing may suggest affiliation.
The logo is a raster with a light halo on white. It needs a transparent or SVG file and a compact header lockup before build.
Mock data can leak into production. Keep it in one labelled seed file, block launch until it is replaced, and never take real payments in test mode.

The mockup shows recognisable third-party brand packaging (for example detergent, toilet cleaner and tissue brands). Showing them needs the right from the brand or distributor. Use only photos the owner has the right to show.

assumptions.text: English is the launch language. Layouts tolerate text expansion and RTL, but translated content is not part of v1.
Prices and currency are in Ghana cedis (GHS).
Delivery is within Ghana. Delivery zones and fees are not designed yet.

Belis Bell supplies real product photography before launch; placeholders are used meanwhile. The supplied logo is a raster, so a transparent or SVG version and a horizontal lockup are needed before build.
Usage was set to all day because of heavy contact and ordering, so the store is designed for repeat use as well as first visits.
The announcement bar and trust counter use mock figures for now. Belis Bell must supply the real free-delivery amount and delivery or customer figure before launch.
Category names, Washroom Solutions packs and brand spotlights are mock until the real catalogue and supplier relationships are known.
The address, phone number, email address and opening hours in the mockup are placeholders. They stay mock until Belis Bell supplies the real details.

history.detail: PG-009, PG-017: Selected Fresh and Bright (not editorial) and asked to copy Supply Master's visual style and section arrangement, not content
PG-010, PG-016: Belis Bell logo supplied: brand colours are blue (#006cbc, #044788) and green (#43b14a), not teal
PG-030: Updated logo supplied: descriptor now 'Cleaning Supplies & More, for homes, businesses and institutions'
PG-025, PG-013, PG-029: Owner supplied a home page mockup with its own structure, navigation and green buttons, and will supply all images

gate.notes: I like the way supply master visuals is. Dont copy the content but copy the visual style and the way the sections are arranged
